record.paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For two-dimensional versions of the fourth-order degenerate lubrication equations for a surface-tension-driven film height h, what analytical theory can be developed for existence, regularity, rupture, and asymptotic behavior, given that the one-dimensional theory does not yet extend to two spatial dimensions?

evidence.quote: In 2D, very little is known about these equations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the fourth-order degenerate parabolic equation modeling a thin viscous film driven by surface tension in two spatial dimensions:
  h_t + ∇·( f(h) ∇Δh ) = 0,    x ∈ Ω ⊂ ℝ², t > 0,
where h(x,t) ≥ 0 denotes the film height, f(h) = |h|^n with mobility exponent n > 0, and Ω is either a bounded domain (with suitable no-flux/zero-contact-angle boundary conditions) or the torus 𝕋². Initial data h(x,0) = h₀(x) ≥ 0 is prescribed with h₀ ∈ H¹(Ω).

Develop an analytical theory for this two-dimensional problem addressing the following items:
(a) Existence of nonnegative weak (and, where possible, strong) solutions for the full range of mobility exponents n > 0.
(b) Regularity properties of weak solutions, including higher Sobolev regularity, positivity sets, and propagation of the support.
(c) Rupture phenomena: determine for which exponents n finite-time singularities (touch-down of h to zero) can occur, and characterize the local structure (e.g. self-similar profiles) of such singularities.
(d) Long-time asymptotic behavior of global solutions, including convergence to equilibria (constants, droplets) and convergence rates.

Specifically, extend the one-dimensional theory of nonnegative weak solutions, entropy/energy dissipation estimates, finite-speed-of-propagation results, and rupture analysis to the genuinely two-dimensional setting.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists: weak existence and some long-time-behavior results for the multi-dimensional thin-film equation have been established (e.g., Bertozzi–Pugh and subsequent work, including results on convergence to mean and entropy methods). However, a complete two-dimensional theory matching the one-dimensional results — covering the full range of mobility exponents, sharp regularity, finite-speed-of-propagation, and rupture/singularity analysis — remains incomplete. Surveys note that "in 2D, very little is known" relative to the 1D case, although several pieces have been filled in over the past two decades.

status_evidence.title: The lubrication approximation for thin viscous films: Regularity and long-time behavior of weak solutions
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous weak existence theory presented for all n > 0; solutions become strong positive after finite time and converge to their means.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-dimensional existence and long-time behavior partially established for the thin-film equation.

status_evidence.title: Viscous Thin Films (MPI MIS project page)
status_evidence.snippet: Research program studying analytic properties (existence, regularity, asymptotics) of thin-film equations in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research effort indicates the higher-dimensional theory is not yet complete.

status_evidence.title: The lubrication approximation for thin viscous films: the moving contact line with a porous media cutoff
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses rupture/finite-time singularities and the structure of weak solutions for thin-film equations.
status_evidence.claim: Rupture phenomena are studied primarily in one dimension; full 2D rupture analysis remains open.
